sections.body: Block code lets you build programs by snapping blocks together, like LEGO for computers. 🧱
A SEQUENCE is blocks in order: 'move 10 steps' → 'turn right' → 'say Hello!'
The computer runs the blocks from top to bottom, one at a time.
Try a free block-coding app (like ScratchJr) with a grown-up. Make a character walk and wave!
ScratchJr and Code.org are free. Let your child explain their program to you. That's great learning.

quiz.q: In what order does the computer run blocks?
options: Top to bottom, one at a time
hints: It starts with the first block.
A recipe is followed step 1, step 2, step 3. Blocks are run the same way.
quiz.explain: Blocks run from top to bottom, one at a time.

quiz.q: You want a cat to walk, then jump. Which order?
hints: The order of blocks is the order of actions.
To wave then smile, put the wave block first. Do the same for walk and jump.
quiz.explain: Put the walk block first, then the jump block.
